source.note: Identity and full byte comparisons establish equality; hashes only summarize those same buffers. Normal vendor material version/listener bookkeeping is not treated as a source edit.

ownedDrain.note: Event-driven QA-owned cleanup bookkeeping only. Register each owned Promise before wait, or synchronously/asynchronously within a retirement that has not yet completed. Promise/thenable identity is deduplicated across this tracker: only its first accepted retirement runs. A fulfilled/rejected producer is not complete until its retirement (including any returned Promise and newly registered followers) finishes. Producer rejection alone is not a cleanup failure. Capacity is a lifetime entry bound, including completed entries; rejected capacity registrations are not observed and remain the caller's cleanup responsibility. The first wait uses one overall deadline with no polling and returns one fixed immutable report. Timeout does not cancel producer/retirement Promises; already accepted and later capacity-eligible followers continue best-effort, and later snapshots may differ from that fixed wait result. Work registered after an already completed wait cannot retroactively change its result. Reports retain primitive labels/status only, not values, raw errors, resources or Promises. This tracker performs no rendering, Game, storage or GPU operation.

note: QA-only optional upper-body candidate, never a natural-motion or new-animation claim. Twelve final bosses use controlled actors and original512 native rendering; boss01final covers16 angles and the other11 cover4, with identical seven windup/attack phases in Aoriginal/Bcandidate. These840 active samples and separate inactive idle/walk/death controls are correctness work, not performance/FPS measurements or12 actual fights. Hands use an original geometry vertex dominated by its forearm skin weight when available; any joint fallback is explicitly qualified. The10% body-alpha-height travel target is an initial visual-QA flag, not an anatomical or gameplay guarantee. Full geometry/index/UV/skin-attribute bytes are compared at each model boundary, with original geometry/material/map/source identities preserved. One own model/two atlases and one contact sheet are retained at a time. The caller-facing main renderer is never assigned; all images and GPU contexts here are owned and retired. Already-started GLTF/Image loads cannot be cancelled; late completion cleanup is scheduled. Original source-file SHAs are separately verified evidence, not rehashed by this browser helper. Separate opt-in qa-boss-owned-cleanup=1 owned-lifecycle route. Legacy action QA is unchanged. Registered subsets are explicitly reported by selectedBossKeys/fullCatalogue and actual activeSamples/inactiveSamples; the840-sample catalogue description above applies only to the full catalogue, and omitted bosses remain unverified. The same original render, phases, hand-travel thresholds and pixel/source checks are retained. Every known owned registry/model/atlas Promise is registered before its await, and retirement can discover followers. Each owned atlas/model await has a separate15second timeout; the one overall15second event-driven cleanup deadline starts only in finalization. These deadlines do not cancel native loads or bound the complete correctness job. Original progress/image callback awaits are cancellation-raced, not a new globally timed caller-callback scheduler. Resource disposal and source-image close are attempted once per owned identity. Final maps, CPU/GPU helpers, surfaces and main-owner descriptors are inspected after the drain. Timeout/failure returns a fixed primitive snapshot; late accepted handlers still retire best-effort without changing that report. No Game/storage writes, source edits, performance measurements or product adoption. Current final12 registry models have no secondary walkFile loader graph; this cleanup proof does not cover unrelated loader internals.
